tour.take: Take a tour of this page

common.findBody: Type to search, and narrow the list with the filters next to it.

overview.welcome: Payrudder measures what your customers use, prices it with your packages, bills it and collects the payment. This short tour shows you around.
overview.apps: An app is one product you bill for. Open one from here to see its dashboard, customers and billing.
overview.groups: Everything you can open is listed here. Inside an app, the sidebar grows into customers, billing, growth, developers and settings.
overview.sandbox: Every app has a sandbox to try things with test money and a live environment for real payments. This switch picks which one you look at.
overview.account: Switch organisation, open your settings or sign out from your menu.
overview.again: Every page has this icon. Press it any time for a short tour of the page you are on.

dashboard.intro: The dashboard of one app in one environment: payments, invoices, subscriptions and customers over the period you choose.
dashboard.figures: Choose the period and the currency at the top; every figure and chart follows. Currencies are never added together.

goLive.intro: The live environment starts switched off: no live keys, no real charges. Finish the checklist, then switch it on.
goLive.checklist: Each item says what is missing and takes you to where you fix it. When all are done, an owner can activate live.

apiKeys.intro: API keys let your server talk to Payrudder. Sandbox keys act on test data, live keys on real data.
apiKeys.create: Create a key for the sandbox to start. The secret is shown once, so copy it then. You can rotate or revoke a key at any time.

sandbox.intro: Tools that act on the sandbox only: start again from a clean slate, and choose how test payments end.
sandbox.scenarios: Pick an outcome (paid, declined, an error that clears on retry) to see how your integration copes before real money is involved.

appSettings.intro: What this app was created with. Its currency and time zone decide how invoices are worked out, so they are fixed once the app exists.

members.intro: Who belongs to this organisation, their roles and the invitations that are still open.
members.invite: Invite a colleague by e-mail and choose their role. Viewers can look but not change anything.

settings.intro: Your organisation's name, your profile and how the console looks for you.

partner.intro: The partner portal: your referral links, the customers you brought and the commission you have earned.

paymentProviders.intro: Connect the payment providers your customers pay through, once for all apps or app by app.
paymentProviders.cards: Each card shows whether a provider is connected and works. Open one to connect, test or disconnect it.
paymentProviders.sandboxTitle: Nothing to connect in the sandbox
paymentProviders.sandbox: The sandbox runs against a built-in simulator, so you can try everything without a provider account.

customers.intro: The people and companies you bill. Open a customer to see their invoices, payments, subscriptions and credits.
customers.create: Add a customer by hand. Customers are also created by your API when they sign up in your product.

subscriptions.intro: Which customer is on which package, and in what state: trialing, active, past due, paused or cancelled.
subscriptions.create: Start a subscription for a customer. You can give it a free trial with no card, or leave the package's own trial in place.

usage.intro: What your customers used, by meter and by customer, in the period you pick, against their limits.
usage.tabs: Switch between the overview, the meters and the customers.

credits.intro: Prepaid credits: the packs you sell, and each customer's balance and history.
credits.packs: Credit packs are credits sold for a price. A customer buys one through a payment link.
credits.grant: Choose a customer to see their balance. From here, or from their customer page, grant free credits with a reason and an optional expiry.

meters.intro: A meter says what is measured and how usage events add up: a count, a sum or a maximum.
meters.create: Add a meter, or a new version of an existing one. Packages price the meters you make.

packages.intro: What customers subscribe to: a fixed fee, prices for the usage you meter, and limits.
packages.create: Publish a package or a new version of one. A package can include a free trial, or be a free tier with limits only.
packages.trials: Give a package a default trial in days, and subscriptions to it start trialing with no card. A free tier is a package with no fee and limits only.

pricing.intro: Payment-retry delays and tax rates: what happens when a charge is declined, and what is added to what you bill.
pricing.tabs: Switch between the sections of this page.

coupons.intro: Discounts: a coupon says what is taken off, and customers get it through a promotion code.
coupons.create: Create a coupon, then add codes for it. Each code can have its own limit and expiry.

invoices.intro: Every invoice, with its state: open, paid, void or uncollectible.
invoices.list: Open a row to see its lines, payments and credit notes. Invoices are made for you at the end of each billing period.

payments.intro: Every attempt to collect money, with the provider, the amount and what came of it.
payments.list: Open a payment to see which invoice it was for and what the provider said.

paymentLinks.intro: Links a customer opens to pay without signing in: for an open invoice, a fixed amount or a credit pack.
paymentLinks.list: Your links and their state. A link stops working when it expires or is revoked.

accounting.intro: What you earned from paid invoices and what you spent, for the period you choose.
accounting.currencies: Each currency is shown on its own. Amounts in different currencies are never added together or converted.

reports.intro: Revenue, subscriptions and unpaid invoices, month by month.
reports.table: Each currency has its own rows; amounts in different currencies are never added together.

affiliates.intro: Run a partner programme: partners get a link and a code, and earn a commission on what the customers they bring pay.
affiliates.tabs: The sections go from the programme's terms to partners, commissions and payouts.

webhooks.intro: Payrudder sends a signed message to your server when something happens: an invoice is paid, a subscription changes.
webhooks.create: Add an HTTPS endpoint and choose the events it wants. The signing secret is shown once.

mail.intro: Choose which e-mails Payrudder sends to your customers on your behalf.
mail.categories: Switch a kind of e-mail on or off. A kind that is off is dropped, not queued.

tenants.intro: Every tenant on the platform, for operators.
tenants.list: Open one to see its customers, billing and settings as the tenant sees them.

playground.intro: A guided walk through the whole flow in a throwaway account: meter, plan, usage, the close of the period and the invoice.

deadLetters.intro: Messages the platform could not process after several tries, for operators to inspect and replay.

welcome.title: Bill for what your customers use
welcome.body: Payrudder measures usage, prices it with your packages, bills it and collects the payment. Set up your first pieces now, in a sandbox where nothing is real.

meter.title: Meter usage
meter.body: Send events: API calls, gigabytes, seats, tokens.

price.title: Price it
price.body: Packages with a fixed fee, usage prices and limits.

bill.title: Bill it
bill.body: Invoices are made for you at the end of each period.

paid.title: Get paid
paid.body: Customers pay through the providers you connect.

organisation.title: Your organisation
organisation.body: The name your team and customers see, and the defaults for your first app.
organisation.name: Organisation name
organisation.note: The currency and the time zone decide how invoices are worked out, so they cannot be changed once the app exists.

app.title: Your first app
app.body: An app is one product you bill for. It comes with a sandbox to test in and a live environment for real payments.
app.name: App name

meter.title: What do you measure?
meter.body: A meter turns usage events into a quantity you can bill. Pick a template; you can add or change meters later.

api_calls.name: API calls
api_calls.body: Counts every request your customers make.

storage.name: Storage (GB)
storage.body: The most storage a customer used in the period.

seats.name: Seats
seats.body: The most seats a customer had in the period.

tokens.name: AI tokens
tokens.body: Adds up the tokens your customers spend.

package.title: Your first package
package.body: A package is what a customer subscribes to: a fixed monthly fee plus a price for each unit they use.
package.name: Package name
package.note: You can add limits, other currencies and a free trial on the Packages page.

event.title: Send a test event
event.body: We create a test customer, subscribe it to your package and send one usage event to your sandbox, so you see the whole path work.
event.sent: Accepted: {quantity} {unit} of usage in your sandbox.

done.title: You are all set
done.body: Your sandbox has a meter, a package and its first usage event. Here is what usually comes next.

dashboard.title: Open your sandbox dashboard
dashboard.body: See the usage and the invoice the test event leads to.

keys.title: Create an API key
keys.body: Let your own server send usage.

team.title: Invite your team
team.body: Colleagues can join with a role of their own.

live.title: Go live
live.body: Connect a payment provider and switch real billing on.

items.package: Publish a package with a price

scope.allHint: The {env} data of every app in one table. Open a row to work on it in its own app.
scope.noData: No app has anything here yet.
scope.chooseTitle: This page works on one app at a time
scope.chooseHint: Choose the app whose {page} you want to open.

saas.title: Plan and billing
saas.intro: The plan of this organisation, what it uses of it, and the invoices Payrudder issued for it.
saas.disabled: Plans are not enabled on this installation: nothing is limited.
saas.readOnly: Only an owner or an administrator can change the plan.

confirm.title: Move to {plan}?
confirm.upgrade: The plan costs {price}. The change applies at once.
confirm.downgrade: The change applies at once. It is refused when your usage does not fit the smaller limits; nothing is deleted.

admin.title: Organisations
admin.intro: Every organisation with its plan and usage. An override puts one on a plan without a checkout or gives it limits of its own.
admin.search: Search by name or owner address
admin.sheetIntro: Change the plan without a checkout, or set limits of this organisation's own.
admin.limitsHint: Limits: a whole number, 0 for unlimited. Leave a field empty to keep it as it is.
admin.badLimit: A limit is a whole number from 0 up.
